items.item_text: Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.

Provides advice and assistance to students on all aspects of their academic experience, including progression and requirement matters for the 2-3 faculty departments/School/campus-wide General Education. Identifies students with GPA or progress problems, advises students, and recommends appropriate courses of action by the major or School (e.g., academic probation, dismissal, Normal Progress Policy). Determines barriers, distractions, and complications affecting a student's academic success, helps students recognize these key non-academic issues, and makes appropriate referrals for additional therapeutic counseling and/or assistance from other units. Advises students on a wide range of course possibilities and/or ways to complete degree requirements that may not be clearly defined. Determines transferability and applicability of non-UC courses and/or courses of the organization within or outside of the department that may affect ongoing requirements.

Responsible for onboarding of traditional students into the School of Social Sciences, Humanities, and Arts (SSHA), including but not limited to transition activities, processes, events, and programs. Researches, develops, plans, and executes School activities & initiatives for students in transition, including but not limited to Welcome Week planning, New Student Orientation programming, 2
year student transition, and JumpStart Your 3rd Year initiatives.

Works closely with the SSHA Academic Advising Peer Navigator program, which consists of at least 6 undergraduate students who provide peer-to-peer support to continuing SSHA students on a range of topics, including but not limited to: academic success, degree completion planning, course scheduling, on-campus and off-campus resources, university, and School policies. Works closely with SSHA Academic Advising Student Assistants and the Student Services Assistant to ensure students' experience when visiting SSHA Academic Advising reception is a safe and welcoming space for all students.

Advises new and continuing instructors on student advising issues. Provides faculty referrals to the appropriate offices, including the Office of Student Conduct and the Dean of Students Office. Advises new and continuing instructors on major, School, and university policies and procedures. Assists faculty in determining course scheduling needs for student progression to graduation. Participates in planning academic curriculum in collaboration with the department chair and faculty, and with other departments, to ensure students' progress through course sequences, avoid conflicts, and ensure compliance with organization-wide policies.
Manages the School of Social Sciences, Humanities, and Arts (SSHA) Academic Advising website and social media accounts.
Other duties as assigned. Includes responding to other unanticipated advising support questions, inquiries, and needs. May supervise student employees.
Advanced degree from an accredited university in Counseling, Higher Education, Student Affairs, or a related area. (Preferred)
